docs.title: AHEAD User Manual
docs.text: This manual explains how to navigate the AHEAD platform and how to enter, assess and consult data on events, assets, damage and losses.

docs.title: What you can do in AHEAD
docs.text:
The platform is organised into six sections, all reached from the sidebar:

Section What it is for Dashboard Overview of the data collected, with a map of reported damage locations. Events Register and manage the events that cause damage, such as storms, floods or earthquakes. Owner Profiles Register the individuals or organisations that own or manage the assets. Baseline Information Describe the assets and their elements before any damage, that is, their exposure characteristics. Damage & Loss Assessment Record and classify the damage and losses suffered by registered assets during an event. Queries & Reporting Retrieve, filter and analyse the stored information through queries and dashboards.

docs.title: Order of work
docs.text:
The sections depend on each other. A damage record can only point to an element, an asset, an owner and an event that already exist in the database. When entering new data, work in this order:

  1. Register the owner in Owner Profiles, so it can be linked to the asset.
  2. Register the asset in Baseline Information and link it to its owner.
  3. Catalogue the asset's elements in Elements & Production. Only elements listed here can be selected as damaged later.
  4. Register the event in Events, if it is not in the database yet.
  5. Create a survey in Damage & Loss Assessment that links the event and the asset.
  6. Record the damage to each element, and any economic losses.
  7. Consult the results in Queries & Reporting.

Reusing records

Owners, assets and events only need to be registered once. The same asset can be surveyed again after a later event, so you do not need to create a new asset record for each survey.

docs.title: Example data
docs.text: The platform already contains data from the testbeds run during the project. The Regione Lombardia example shows how a complete case, from event to damage, is recorded.

docs.title: Queries & Reporting
docs.text:
The Queries & Reporting section is where you retrieve, filter and analyse the information stored in the AHEAD database.

The other sections are mostly for entering and managing data. This one is for consulting and analysing data already in the platform. Its dashboards support the analysis of damage and of the related costs.

The Queries & Reporting menu.

The section has two tools:

  • Damage Query: the damage recorded for an event, on a map and in a table.
  • Event Cost Analysis: the economic consequences of an event and how its costs are distributed.

docs.title: Damage Query
docs.text: Damage Query retrieves the damage information linked to a specific event.

docs.title: Selecting an event
docs.text:
Start by selecting an event from the list. The platform then builds a dashboard with an overview of the damage recorded for that event.

The dashboard shows three indicators:

  • Total Damages
  • Estimated Costs
  • Approved Costs

They are calculated from the information entered in the data-entry and assessment sections.

The Damage Query dashboard.

docs.title: Filtering and consulting the records
docs.text:
Once an event is selected, you can narrow the results by asset type to focus on one category of assets and its damage records.

Below the map, a table lists the individual records and their details. Use it to examine the damage records stored in the database for the selected event and filters.

docs.title: Event Cost Analysis
docs.text:
Event Cost Analysis is a second view of the stored information that focuses on the economic consequences of events.

The filters are like those in Damage Query. The dashboard, however, processes the data differently and gives more weight to the analysis and distribution of costs. Use it to explore the economic information linked to an event and to examine the cost data that match your filters.

The Event Cost Analysis dashboard.

docs.title: Damage & Loss Assessment
docs.text:
The Damage & Loss Assessment section is where you record and classify the damage and losses suffered by the assets registered in Baseline Information.

It is laid out like Baseline Information. A sidebar menu, organised by sector, leads to the sub-sections.

The Damage & Loss Assessment menu.

docs.title: Surveys
docs.text:
All assessment work is organised in surveys. A survey brings together, for one assessment:

  • the event that caused the damage,
  • the asset being assessed,
  • the owner or managing organisation of the asset,
  • the date of the survey.

The event, asset and owner are taken from records that already exist. Only the survey date is entered when the survey is created.

The upper part of the page lists the surveys already registered. Select a survey to view its details or to edit it.

docs.title: Creating a survey
docs.text:
1. Open the sector's page in Damage & Loss Assessment and click New.

  2. Select the asset (in this example, a farm) that you registered in Baseline Information.

    Selecting the asset to assess.

  3. Select the event from those already registered in the database.

    Selecting the event.

  4. Enter the survey date.

  5. Check the information and click Save.

The new survey record is now created. Next, record the damage.

docs.title: Recording damage
docs.text: The damage assessment itself takes place in the Damages page of a survey. Open it once the survey exists and its Info page is complete (see Creating a survey).

docs.title: Creating a damage record
docs.text:
1. Open the survey.
  2. Go to the Damages page.
  3. Click New to create a damage record.

  4. Select the damaged element. The list contains the elements registered for this asset in Elements & Production.

    Selecting the damaged element.

  5. Select the damage type.

  6. Fill in the fields that appear, with the characteristics of the damage and the assessment information.
  7. Save the damage record.

Because the elements come from the asset's own inventory, every damage record is linked to the right asset and component.

docs.title: Classifying the damage
docs.text:
The first choice is the type of damage to the selected element. The platform then shows the fields and options needed to describe and classify that type of damage.

Choosing the damage category.

The form is dynamic. The fields on the right-hand side depend on the element and on the damage category selected, so different elements and categories ask for different assessment information. Review these fields carefully and fill in those that apply to the damage you are recording.

For example, the People, Functionality and Not structural categories show these fields:

People: number of dead, injured and missing. Functionality. Not structural: choosing the non-structural element.

docs.title: More than one type of damage to the same element
docs.text:
One element can suffer more than one type of damage. A barn, for example, may have both structural and functional damage.

In that case, create a separate damage record for each type, all pointing to the same element. Each record then has its own classification and assessment information. This keeps each damage mechanism, and its consequences, documented on its own.

docs.title: Sendai indicators
docs.text:
You can link each damage record to an indicator of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction. Where one applies, select it in the Sendai indicator field when you fill in the record.

Selecting a Sendai indicator.

docs.title: Damage causality
docs.text:
You can also record that one damage caused another. For example, primary damage to one component may lead to secondary damage to another component.

In the Caused by table, tick the damage record that caused the one you are entering. Damage records are then linked to each other instead of being treated as unrelated.

Recording which damage caused this one.

docs.title: Economic losses
docs.text:
Besides physical damage, a survey can record the economic losses linked to the event and the affected asset.

Economic losses recorded in a survey.

To add one, click Add New Economic Loss and fill in the window that opens.

The Add New Economic Loss window.

Fill in the fields with the information available from the survey, or from official documents received later.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The Events section is where you create and manage the events that may cause damage and losses to the assets surveyed in AHEAD.

An event can be a storm, flood, tornado, hurricane, wildfire, earthquake, drought or landslide. The platform can also classify multi-hazard events.

The Events page.

The page has two areas:

  • The events list at the top shows the events already registered in the database.
  • The event form below it is where you enter a new event or change an existing one.

docs.title: The events list
docs.text:
You can find an event in two ways:

  • type its name in the search field, or
  • filter the list by event type: tornado, storm, hurricane, flood, wildfire, earthquake, drought, landslide or multi-hazard event.

The table lists the registered events and their main characteristics:

Column Content Name The name given to the event, for example Storm Kristin, Saxony Flood July 2021 (Bernd), Saxony Flood August 2002 or Saxony Flood June 2013. Type The event type. Multi-Hazard Whether the event is part of a multi-hazard occurrence. Date The recorded date of the event. Action Buttons to edit or delete the event.

docs.title: Creating a new event
docs.text:
1. Click New in the upper-right corner of the Events page.
  2. Enter the name of the event.
  3. Select the event type from the drop-down menu. To register a multi-hazard event itself, choose Multi-Hazard Event as the type.

  4. If the event is part of a multi-hazard occurrence that is already in the database, tick the multi-hazard option and select that occurrence from the list.

    Linking an event to a registered multi-hazard event.

  5. Enter the date of the event.

  6. Define where the event happened, in one of two ways:
    • type the address in the address fields, or
    • draw the affected area on the interactive map.
  7. Check that the information is complete and correct.
  8. Click Save to register the event.

The drawing tools on the map let you mark the event area as a polyline, a polygon, a rectangle, a circle or a marker. You can also edit or delete what you have drawn.

The map drawing tools.

Once saved, the event appears in the events list. You will select it later, mainly when you create a survey in Damage & Loss Assessment.

docs.title: Owner Profiles
docs.text:
The Owner Profiles section is where you create and manage information on the individuals or organisations that own or manage the surveyed assets.

An owner is not only a private property owner. It can also be an institution, a company or the organisation that manages the asset.

Register owners first

Register the owner before you create the asset in Baseline Information. You can then link the right owner or managing organisation to each asset.

The Owner Profiles page.

The page has two areas:

  • The owner profiles list shows the profiles already registered in the database.
  • The profile form is where you create a new profile or change an existing one.

docs.title: Creating an owner profile
docs.text:
1. Fill in the fields:

    Field Content Full Name Name of the individual, institution or managing organisation. Fiscal Code Tax identification or fiscal code of the owner or organisation. Email Contact email address. Phone Contact telephone number.

  2. Check that the details are correct and belong to the person or organisation linked to the asset.

  3. Click Save.

The new profile then appears in the owner profiles list.

docs.title: Editing and reusing profiles
docs.text: You can select an existing profile from the list and change it when needed. Saved profiles can be reused whenever you create or update an asset record, so the same owner does not have to be entered twice.

docs.title: Baseline Information
docs.text:
The Baseline Information section is where you register and manage the information that describes the surveyed assets.

This information records the exposure characteristics of each asset: its physical, functional and operational characteristics before any damage assessment takes place.

Damage & Loss Assessment builds on it later. The assets and elements registered here are the ones you select when you record which parts of an asset an event damaged.

docs.title: Sectors
docs.text:
The platform groups assets by sector. The sectors currently available are:

  • Economic Activities
    • Farms
    • Businesses
  • Lifelines
    • Telecommunication
    • Electrical infrastructure
    • Transport infrastructure
  • Built Environment
The sectors in the Baseline Information menu.

Sectors under development

Water systems, defence infrastructure and disaster waste are under development. The list of sectors may change as the platform develops further.

docs.title: Surveying the same asset more than once
docs.text:
The same asset can be surveyed more than once. This lets you follow damage to one asset over time, for example when it is hit by different events or assessed repeatedly.

You therefore do not need to create a new asset record for each survey. Retrieve the existing asset and reuse its information.

docs.title: Working with assets
docs.text:
The next pages use a farm as the example:

  1. Registering a farm: enter the general information and link the owner.
  2. Elements & Production: catalogue the elements and production lines of the asset.

docs.title: Elements & Production
docs.text:
The Elements & Production page is where you register the individual components, structures or production lines of an asset.

Catalogue every damaged component

The elements registered here form the reference list used in Damage & Loss Assessment. A component missing from this list cannot be recorded as damaged. Make sure every damaged component of the surveyed asset is catalogued.

The Elements & Production page.

The page lists the elements already registered for the asset. Each row has actions to edit or delete the element, depending on your permissions.

docs.title: Creating an element
docs.text:
1. Open the Elements & Production page and click New.

  2. Select the element category from the Type list.

    Choosing the element type.

  3. Fill in the fields that appear.

  4. Enter the characteristics needed to classify the exposure of the element.
  5. Where available, draw the position of the element on the map with the drawing tools.
  6. Check the information.
  7. Click Save.

The form changes with the element type. Each category asks for the information needed to describe its own exposure characteristics.

docs.title: Registering a farm
docs.text:
Farms belong to the Economic Activities sector. Open Baseline Information → Economic Activities → Farm in the sidebar to see the list of farms already in the database.

Check the list before you create a new farm. If the farm is already registered, reuse it instead of creating a duplicate (see Surveying the same asset more than once).

To register a new farm, click New. Data entry is split across three pages, shown as tabs at the top of the form.

docs.title: Step 1 – Info
docs.text:
Fill in the Info page with the general information and characteristics of the farm.

The Info page of a farm.

docs.title: Step 2 – Owner/Managing Organisation
docs.text: Open the Owner/Managing Organisation page. Link the farm to an owner or managing organisation that you registered earlier in Owner Profiles. Selecting an existing profile connects the asset to its ownership or management information.

docs.title: Step 3 – Elements & Production
docs.text:
Open the Elements & Production page and catalogue the individual elements or production lines of the farm.

Do not skip this step. Only the elements registered here can be selected in Damage & Loss Assessment. The page is described in Elements & Production.

docs.title: Example: the Regione Lombardia testbed
docs.text:
The Regione Lombardia event was one of the first testbeds set up in AHEAD. It shows how information on a hazard event, the exposed assets and the resulting damage and losses can be recorded, organised and analysed in the AHEAD database.

The Lombardia event as recorded in the AHEAD database.

Owner profiles are fictitious

The owner profiles in the testbed contain fictitious information. Owner details are mandatory when registering an asset, so made-up data were used instead of real personal or organisational information. These profiles are for demonstration and testing only and do not match real owners or managing organisations.

The screenshots below follow the records for the transport sector, from the description of the exposed assets to the recording of damage and losses.

docs.title: Baseline Information
docs.text: Transport assets and their general information. The owner assigned to a transport asset. The elements of a transport asset.

docs.title: Damage & Loss Assessment
docs.text: Surveys of transport assets for the Lombardia event. A damage record for a transport asset.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Dashboard gives a first overview of the data collected through AHEAD. At present it shows the information from the testbeds run during the project.

The Dashboard.

Its main component is an interactive map of the reported damage locations. Use it to see where impacts were recorded, find areas with reported damage and filter the records by category.

docs.title: Navigating the map
docs.text: Tool What it does Zoom in (+) Shows a smaller area in more detail. Zoom out (−) Shows a wider area. Click and drag Moves the map. Damage markers Coloured circles mark the locations linked to recorded damage.

docs.title: The information panel
docs.text:
An information panel sits in the upper-right corner of the map. It contains filters and indicators that help you read the map.

The information panel. Filter by type

Shows only the damage records from one sector of affected assets: Farm, Business, Telecommunication, Electrical, Transport or Built Environment.

The Filter by type menu.

Visible damages The number of damage records currently visible on the map. Coloured counters The number of records for each case study, that is, each testbed run during the project. Each colour stands for one case study. Position accuracy

How precisely each damage location is known:

  • Exact position: the location was identified precisely.
  • Approximate position: the location is an estimate and may not match an exact point.
Zoom in for detailed markers More markers and more detailed information appear as you zoom in. Details of a damage record after zooming in.

Combining the map tools with the filters gives a detailed picture of where impacts occurred and what AHEAD has recorded about them.

docs.title: Platform layout
docs.text:
The sidebar on the left of the interface is the main navigation menu. It gives access to every section of the platform.

The sidebar.

The sidebar contains the following sections:

Dashboard An overview of the data collected through AHEAD, with the geographical distribution of reported damage locations. See Dashboard. Events Manage the events linked to the recorded damage, including event type, dates and location. See Events. Owner Profiles Create and manage profiles of the owners or managing organisations of the surveyed assets. An owner can be an individual, an institution or an organisation responsible for an asset. See Owner Profiles. Baseline Information Enter and manage the information that describes the surveyed assets. This is their exposure characteristics, and it is the reference dataset for later damage and loss assessments. See Baseline Information. Damage & Loss Assessment Record and classify the damage and losses linked to previously registered assets and events. See Damage & Loss Assessment. Queries & Reporting Retrieve, filter and analyse the information in the AHEAD database through dedicated queries and reporting dashboards. See Queries & Reporting.
